purpose: Test new/reuse/separate decisions and exact graph attachment on existing extracted operations; not a new extraction trial or a semantic-accuracy benchmark.

cases.decision_explanation: Assign the selected version 1 bead-bound ChIPmentation reaction to a new, specifically bounded Tn5 tagmentation concept. Direct packet evidence supports the substrate, fragmentation/adapter-tagging mechanism, pre-recovery output, and sequencing-library purpose. No existing concepts are present in the frozen registry. The assignment contains only the host-bound selected occurrence and retains the limits on commercial reagent internals and molecular-end chemistry; unrelated workflow-wide gaps do not prevent this transformation-level interpretation.
cases.distinction: The frozen registry has an empty concepts object, and all eight actual lookups by operation name, transformation, and substrate returned no candidates. Consequently there was no existing definition available to inspect or reuse; this is a new registry entry, not a claim of literature novelty. The source explicitly distinguishes ChIPmentation on bead-bound immunoprecipitated chromatin from ChIP-tagmentation of purified ChIP DNA. It also distinguishes Tn5 fragmentation/adapter tagging from conventional multistep end repair, A-tailing, and adapter ligation. Accessibility profiling of unenriched intact chromatin has a different input selection context. This definition therefore preserves both the reported Tn5 mechanism and the antibody-enriched bead-bound substrate. Membership does not imply that recipes or transposomes are interchangeable. The observed member is the original version 1 Nextera reaction; its exact loaded strands and end chemistry remain unspecified, and proposed chromatin-protein protection is not used to establish the shared mechanism.
cases.review_rationale: The sole proposed member, o_tag_v1, satisfies the whole definition at the selected s_prepared_v1 to s_tagged_v1 boundary. Main p00003 explicitly identifies ChIPmentation as Tn5 library preparation on bead-bound chromatin; p00004 explicitly defines hyperactive-Tn5 tagmentation as simultaneous fragmentation and adapter tagging. These statements, the actual Nextera reaction in p00016, and the bead-bound adapter-introduction statement in supplement p00005 establish the mechanism for this substrate without substituting endpoint similarity for mechanistic evidence. Supplement p00039 establishes the version 1 antibody IP and bead-capture context; main p00016 places two cold Tris washes before the 30 microliter Tris/MgCl2 reaction with 1 microliter kit enzyme for 10 minutes at 37 degrees C, followed by bead washes, elution, reverse-crosslinking and purification. Thus substrate, transformation, immediate retained output, conditions and downstream purpose are supported. Retained antibody-enrichment provenance is an inference from this material route, not a claim that tagging creates specificity or quantitatively preserves every enriched molecule. The inhibitory-carryover description is supported at the contextual level by the reported removal of detergent/salts/EDTA before reaction and the author protocol's explicit use of SDS/EDTA to inactivate/strip transposase afterward; no concentration-dependent inhibition rule is established. Main p00018 places nick translation and amplification downstream. The name and scope preserve bead-bound IP context, exclude the separately documented purified-DNA and conventional ligation routes, and distinguish accessibility profiling without importing its recipe. There are no aliases to assess. The member rationale correctly treats chromatin-protein protection as the authors' reasoning, rather than a universal mechanistic requirement. Enzyme stock activity/concentration, original loaded adapter strands and exact covalent intermediates are not specified by the inspected reaction descriptions; their omission does not defeat this intentionally limited transformation category. The empty frozen registry and eight independently repeated lookups provide no existing definition to reuse or compare; the source-based distinctions justify this new indexing category without asserting literature novelty or recipe interchangeability.

cases.decision_explanation: The registered primary and supplementary passages support a useful mechanistic assignment for the single selected standard transposition occurrence. The inspected registry definition is incompatible with its native-nuclear substrate and accessibility information effect, so a separate concept is proposed. Unresolved adapter-end chemistry and reaction-reagent internals remain explicit and do not imply missing evidence for the reported Tn5 fragmentation/tagging mechanism. Workflow-wide amplification, quantitation, sequencing and computational gaps do not change this selected transformation boundary.
cases.distinction: All three name-, transformation- and purpose-based lookups returned the inspected concept tn5_tagmentation_of_bead_bound_immunoprecipitated_chromatin. That definition requires antibody-enriched chromatin retained on immunoprecipitation beads before elution/crosslink reversal, produces tagged material retaining antibody-enrichment provenance, and explicitly excludes accessibility profiling of unenriched intact chromatin. Here Tn5 acts on native chromatin in unfixed nuclei, and preferential insertion itself encodes accessibility. Sharing the reported Tn5 fragmentation/tagging mechanism does not make the substrate, selection process, output information or required handling compatible with that complete definition. Reuse would require changing its substrate and explicit scope boundary. A separate native-nuclear-accessibility concept therefore fits this occurrence without broadening the frozen definition. This is a new entry relative to the inspected registry candidates, not a claim of literature novelty. Exact adapter/end structures and enzyme/buffer internals remain bounded unknowns; no sequence-level or recipe-level interchangeability is claimed.

cases.review_rationale:
Supported for exactly the proposed transpose_base occurrence, from nuclei_base to tagged_base. The whole definition matches the inspected source: adapter-loaded hyperactive Tn5 simultaneously fragments and tags DNA directly in unfixed nuclei; the source explicitly attributes preferential generation of amplifiable open-chromatin fragments to less probable transposition in sterically hindered chromatin (primary p00004). The standard input is the pellet prepared from 50,000 cells by cold IGEPAL lysis and refrigerated centrifugation (p00015). Immediate resuspension in the reported 25/2.5/22.5 μL TD-buffer/transposase/water mix, 30 minutes at 37 °C, and subsequent Minelute purification are directly reported (p00016). Thus the selected output is the reaction product before purification and amplification, and the claimed 50 μL total is a transparent calculation. These conditions describe the evidenced implementation, not a universal recipe for the category.

The information effect is supported with bounded inference: genomic fragments retain sequence and physical spans that are read out later by sequencing/alignment and paired-end insert sizes (p00006, p00022); accessibility is encoded probabilistically through insertion locations (p00004, p00023). Retaining input-population identity means bulk sample provenance, not cell barcoding. Fragment spans can support subsequent structural interpretation without making nucleosome inference or footprinting part of this reaction. The Figure S4 and S5 claims are accurately limited to the reported local sequence-preference and peak-intensity comparisons (supplement p00007–p00008). They justify retaining sequence preference as part of the measurement, not zero bias, a universal association magnitude, or a compulsory purified-DNA control/correction. The broader wording in primary p00005 does not warrant discarding the more specific moderate-correlation statement in Figure S5.

The definition’s name and purpose follow the explicit Tn5/native-nuclear/accessibility evidence; there are no proposed aliases to substantiate. The scope note correctly starts with prepared nuclei and stops at transposition product, excluding separate preparation, purification, amplification, acquisition and inference operations. Its purified-DNA and antibody-enriched bead-bound exclusions are indexing boundaries, not claims that those substrates cannot undergo Tn5 chemistry. The repair/fill-in exclusion likewise defines this unit; no repair mechanism is inferred from the downstream 72°C incubation in p00017. The known dimer/9-bp insertion geometry in p00023 is compatible with leaving complete adapter/end chemistry unresolved. Supplement p00002 contains PCR-oligo sequences, not an explicit complete Tn5-loaded construct. The reported methods leave TD composition and enzyme stock activity/concentration unspecified. These bounded molecular/recipe gaps do not negate the reported physical mechanism, but they prevent treating this definition as an interchangeable molecular recipe. Other inherited workflow gaps do not alter this selected transformation.

The new-entry distinction is justified against the plausible frozen-registry candidate actually returned by all three supplied lookups and inspected: tn5_tagmentation_of_bead_bound_immunoprecipitated_chromatin requires antibody-enriched bead-bound substrate before elution/crosslink reversal, retains antibody-selection provenance, and expressly excludes unenriched intact-chromatin accessibility profiling. Primary p00004–p00005 and p00015–p00016 establish a different nuclear input and accessibility-dependent selection for this occurrence. Shared Tn5 fragmentation/tagging does not satisfy the existing definition’s complete substrate, output-information and handling requirements. This supports a separate native-nuclear accessibility definition relative to that candidate, without asserting exhaustive registry or literature novelty. The distinct 500/5,000-cell route in p00018 is not reviewed as a member.

cases.decision_explanation: Reuse the existing Tn5 tagmentation of bead-bound immunoprecipitated chromatin concept unchanged for the single host-bound version 2 occurrence. Registered source passages support its substrate, coupled transformation and output boundary; unresolved exact kit strand/end chemistry limits molecular-detail and substitution claims but does not prevent this assignment.
cases.distinction: The inspected bead-bound immunoprecipitated-chromatin definition fits the selected substrate, reported Tn5 fragmentation/tagging mechanism, pre-wash bead-bound output, and adapter introduction into already antibody-enriched DNA without any change. The other inspected hit, tn5_tagmentation_of_native_nuclear_chromatin_for_accessibility_profiling, requires native chromatin in unfixed nuclei and an accessibility-encoding transformation; those requirements do not describe this antibody-enriched bead fraction. A shared enzyme alone does not erase that distinction. Supplement p00005 separately distinguishes bead-bound ChIPmentation from purified-ChIP-DNA tagmentation and conventional multistep library preparation. Version 2's upstream RIPA-LiCl and downstream RIPA washes are branch-specific context around the common tagmentation reaction reported in main p00016, not grounds to broaden the definition or assume complete ChIP recipes are interchangeable. The selected unit excludes those washes and all later recovery, repair and amplification. The copied definition's limits on exact kit strand/end chemistry apply here; enzyme stock activity/concentration and loaded oligos are not supplied, and the proposed protection rationale is not elevated to a general guarantee.

cases.review_rationale:
The sole proposed member, o_tag_v2, satisfies the reused definition at its stated transformation boundary. Main p00003 explicitly identifies ChIPmentation as Tn5-mediated library preparation directly on bead-bound chromatin; main p00004 identifies hyperactive Tn5's coupled fragmentation and adapter tagging. Thus the shared-mechanism assignment has mechanistic evidence beyond an enzyme name or similar endpoint. Main p00016 establishes the immunoprecipitated bead substrate, the version 2 RIPA-LiCl context, two cold Tris washes, and the exact reported reaction: 30 μl of 10 mM Tris pH 8.0/5 mM MgCl2 containing 1 μl Nextera DNA Sample Prep Kit Tagment DNA Enzyme, 10 minutes at 37°C in a thermocycler. Supplement p00040 independently establishes fixed, sonicated chromatin captured on antibody-conjugated Protein A/G beads. The definition's description of inhibitory-buffer removal is an operational inference from the explicit detergent/salt/EDTA-removal wash and the subsequent reaction, with additional source support for SDS/EDTA-mediated transposase inactivation; it does not establish quantitative residual concentrations or a universal inhibition threshold.

Supplement p00005 expressly locates sequencing-adapter introduction on bead-bound chromatin. Main p00016 then handles the beads through version 2 RIPA washes before final washing, elution, crosslink reversal and purification. Together these support the immediate tagged, fragmented bead-associated output before those downstream operations. Retention of upstream target-enrichment provenance is a material-route inference from antibody capture and continued bead handling, not a claim that every tagged fragment remains bound, that enrichment magnitude is unchanged, or that insertion is unbiased. Recovery followed by library amplification is supported by main p00007/p00018; nick translation and PCR are subsequent operations, outside this member.

The definition, shared_mechanism relation, empty aliases and scope note match the inspected frozen concept without expansion. The scope exclusions and distinction are supported: supplement p00005 and main p00015/p00017 distinguish on-bead ChIPmentation from purified-ChIP-DNA tagmentation and conventional end-repair/A-tailing/ligation preparation. The other inspected registry concept requires native chromatin in unfixed nuclei and accessibility encoding; the ATAC source reports those properties, whereas this occurrence acts on fixed, already antibody-enriched chromatin. Version 2's adjacent RIPA-LiCl and RIPA washes remain context around the selected reaction, not additional reviewed members or evidence of recipe interchangeability.

The member rationale and the whole definition are supported at this granularity. Enzyme stock activity/concentration, commercial loaded strands and exact post-insertion covalent ends are not supplied by the inspected reaction descriptions. The inspected delegated oligo inventory is explicitly for PCR and does not resolve those loaded strands. These limits are preserved rather than filled with another kit or inferred sequences. Main p00007 presents chromatin protection as the authors' rationale; universal protection and custom-transposase compatibility are not required or established. Other inherited downstream QC, indexing, control and analysis gaps do not alter this selected tagmentation boundary.
